spots.name: Trieste Cathedral

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Trieste Cathedral, dedicated to Saint Justus, is a Roman Catholic cathedral in Trieste, in northeastern Italy. It is the seat of the Bishop of Trieste.

spots.name: Piazza Unità d'Italia
spots.summary: Piazza Unità d'Italia is the main square in Trieste, a seaport city in northeast Italy. Located at the foot of the hill with the castle of San Giusto, the square faces the Adriatic Sea. It is often said to be Europe's largest square located next to the sea.

spots.name: Risiera di San Sabba
spots.summary: Risiera di San Sabba was a Nazi concentration camp operating in Trieste. Officially designated as a police detention camp (Polizeihaftlager), it was the only one on Italian territory with a crematorium.

spots.summary: Saint Spyridon Serbian Orthodox Church is an Eastern Orthodox church located in Trieste, Italy. It is under jurisdiction of the Serbian Orthodox Eparchy of Switzerland of the Serbian Orthodox Church.

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Grotta Gigante, also known as Riesengrotte or as Grotta di Brisciachi, is a giant cave on the Italian side of the Trieste Karst (Carso), close to the village of Borgo Grotta Gigante or Briščiki in the municipality of Sgonico.

spots.summary: Trieste City Hall is the seat of the city and commune of Trieste in the Italian region of Friuli Venezia Giulia. Situated on the eastern side of Piazza Unità d'Italia, the building serves as the headquarters of the city's administration and is one of the square's most prominent architectural landmarks.

spots.summary: The Revoltella Museum is a modern art gallery founded in Trieste, Italy, in 1872 by Baron Pasquale Revoltella. The baron left his house to the city, including all the artworks, furniture and books it contained.

spots.summary: The Church of Sant'Antonio Taumaturgo, is the main religious building in the Borgo Teresiano in the centre of Trieste as well as the city's largest Catholic church. It stands on a square also known as Sant’Antonio Nuovo, at the end of the Grand Canal.

spots.name: Vittoria Light
spots.summary: Vittoria Light also known as the Victory Lighthouse, is an active lighthouse in Trieste, Italy, serving the Gulf of Trieste. It is located on the Hill of Gretta, off the Strada del Friuli. At a height of 223 feet (68 m) it is one of the tallest lighthouses in the world.

spots.summary: The Arco di Riccardo is a Roman triumphal arch in Trieste, Italy. The 7.2 metre arch is the only remaining part of the city's Roman walls, constructed from 33–32 BC.

spots.summary: The heart of the ancient city of Tergeste. Although only fragmentary remains of the Roman Forum survive—mainly paving, columns, and foundations—the site marks the civic and religious core of Tergeste.

spots.summary: Piazza Venezia is one of the best known squares of Trieste, the capital of Friuli-Venezia Giulia, Italy. The square has a view over the Adriatic to the Alps with the Dolomite Mountains Civetta, Monte Pelmo and Antelao.

spots.name: Canal Grande
spots.summary: Trieste's beautiful grand canal. Step onto the bridge to pose with a bronze statue of James Joyce, one of Trieste's many iconic statues that walk the streets instead of standing on pedestals.

spots.name: Città Vecchia
spots.summary: Trieste boasts an extensive old town: there are many very narrow and crooked streets with typical medieval houses. Nearly the entire area is closed to traffic.

spots.name: Museo di Storia, Arte e Orto Lapidario

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Archaeological, historical and art collections. Prehistoric and protohuman findings of local origin; Roman and medieval sculptures and epigraphs. Egyptian, Greek, Roman and pre-Roman antiques. Numismatic collection. Photograph and book libraries.

spots.name: Orange-ini

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Great for a quick lunch a stone's throw from the square. Arancine are good and have a lot of variety of ingredients. Amazing cannoli freshly prepared. Very informal environment suitable for a quick lunch or a night snack. Possible to consume at the tables outside or take away. Rapidity and smile distinguish this culinary corner of Sicily in the heart of Trieste.

spots.name: La Piadineria

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Quick place to stop in and get some relatively healthy food. Outdoor seating is available. The piadina dough is very good. Good ingredients in general. Excellent choice of flavors. There is another branch of La Piadineria in Via del Ponte, 9/B

spots.name: Trattoria Alla Gioconda

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Family owned trattoria with fresh fish traditionally prepared. Genuine dishes, seasoned with the simplicity of the past to enhance the natural flavor. Generous portions. The owner is very kind. Very casual and optimal quality-to-price ratio.

spots.name: Trattoria Citta Di Pisino

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Trattoria with a characteristic atmosphere, with home cooking, simple but good dishes, fast service. Cucinadomaca is recommended. As soon as you enter, you are catapulted 60/70 years back, typical Triestine cuisine in a vintage setting.

spots.name: Buffet da Siora Rosa

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: One of Trieste's oldest family-owned restaurants operating since before World War II, serving typical Triestine cuisine. Particularly famous for their proscuitto cotto: cooked ham served with piquant mustard and horseradish.

spots.name: Desideri e Auguri Da Marino's

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Excellent little Italian restaurant. The food is like homemade. The best place to have a good meal with dishes that are as alternative as they are delicious. Very friendly owner, quiet and welcoming environment.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Great place for a quick stop for pizza. Excellent pizza mainly take away but there are a few tables to eat it also on site. There are two types of dough, you should try them. Closed Sundays.
